Patients were kept asleep for weeks.
In Montreal from the 1950s, Ewen Cameron kept patients in drug-induced sleep and played them recorded messages on a loop. Part of the work was CIA-funded.

items.caption:
Captive sloths sleep 16 hours. Wild ones don’t.
The first brain recordings of wild three-toed sloths, in Panama, found about 9.6 hours of sleep a day, some six hours less than in captivity.
